3154:     def run_job(self, job_id: str) -> Coroutine[Any, Any, bool]:
3155:         """Manually trigger a job via _run_job_isolated (records history).
3156: 
3157:         A plain ``def`` that returns the coroutine, on purpose: the claim on the
3158:         job -- its ``_RunClaim`` with ``trigger="manual"`` -- is taken HERE,
3159:         synchronously, while the call expression is evaluated. It therefore
3160:         exists before the caller's ``asyncio.create_task`` has scheduled
3161:         anything and before the coroutine's first ``await``. The manual-run
3162:         route answers 409 "already running" off the claim and hands the task it
3163:         creates to ``attach_run_task``, and ``cancel()`` reads the same claim: a
3164:         claim taken only inside the coroutine -- after the offloaded store
3165:         refresh, up to a full lock spin later -- leaves a window in which Cancel
3166:         answers "not running" about a run that Run calls "already running", and
3167:         the run then executes anyway. Loop-only and await-free, so the
3168:         check-and-claim stays atomic against the due-scan and a concurrent
3169:         manual trigger; ``_run_claimed_manual`` releases the claim if the store
3170:         does not hold the job. Every caller awaits or schedules the returned
3171:         coroutine at once (the route wraps it in a task on the same line); one
3172:         that dropped it would leave the job claimed.
3173:         """
3174:         if job_id in self._claims:
3175:             return _manual_run_refused()
3176:         claim = self._claim_run(job_id, "manual")
3177:         return self._run_claimed_manual(job_id, claim)

3511:         which reads loop-owned ``self._claims`` — then runs on the loop

3954:         ``claim`` is this run's claim (see ``_execute_with_timeout``).
3955:         """
3956:         logger.info("Cron: executing '%s' (%s)", job.name, job.id)
3957:         # Reset status for this run so a prior run's "error" can't leak into an
3958:         # "ok" decision below. Same for the fire-time denial marker.
3959:         job.last_status = None
3960:         job.fire_time_denied = False
3961:         job.run_never_started = False
3962:         # Transient retries the callback took this run. The gateway callback only
3963:         # INCREMENTS `_transient_attempts` (a runtime attribute on the live job);
3964:         # this method is the one owner of reading it, clearing it and persisting
3965:         # it -- see the stamp after `last_run_ts` below. The read-and-clear sits
3966:         # in a `finally` so a cancelled or timed-out run (CancelledError skips
3967:         # everything after the await) cannot leak a half-spent budget into the
3968:         # next run's retry allowance.
3969:         retries = 0
3970:         try:
3971:             if self._on_job:
3972:                 try:
3973:                     await self._on_job(job)
3974:                 finally:
3975:                     retries = int(getattr(job, "_transient_attempts", 0) or 0)
3976:                     job._transient_attempts = 0  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

4007:                 if not self._runs.cancelled.has(job.id, claim):
4008:                     job.record_success()
4009:         except Exception as exc:
4010:             job.last_status = "error"
4011:             job.last_error = str(exc)
4012:             logger.error("Cron job '%s' failed: %s", job.name, exc)
4013: 
4014:         job.last_run_ts = time.time()
4015:         # Retry telemetry is stamped HERE, with the `last_run_ts` it describes,
4016:         # so the two can never disagree for a run that completed. Stamping it
4017:         # anywhere inside the callback would bind it to the PREVIOUS run's
4018:         # `last_run_ts` (this line has not run yet while the callback is
4019:         # executing), and the Schedule page -- which shows the count only when
4020:         # the two stamps match -- would never show it. A cancelled run never
4021:         # reaches this line, so its own `last_run_ts` write leaves the pair
4022:         # mismatched and the page shows no count rather than a stale one.
4023:         job.last_retry_count = retries
4024:         job.last_retry_run_ts = job.last_run_ts
4025: 
4026:         # One-shot "at" jobs: disable after the run. A fire-time-DENIED at-job
4027:         # is disabled too — its due time has passed, so leaving it enabled
4028:         # would make it due on EVERY timer tick (a zero-delay refire loop that
4029:         # floods audit/history until resource exhaustion). Parking it disabled
4030:         # (instead of deleting — including the delete_after_run shape, which
4031:         # the merge below retains) keeps it discoverable so an operator can
4032:         # re-enable it after a policy loosening. Recurring jobs are untouched:
4033:         # they simply wait for their next scheduled slot and resume on their
4034:         # own when policy loosens.
4035:         if job.schedule.kind == "at" and (not job.delete_after_run or job.fire_time_denied):
4036:             job.enabled = False

4073:             elif job.id in by_id:
4074:                 apply_run_record(by_id[job.id], job)
4075:             # A fire-time-DENIED run is a policy refusal, not a completed run:
4076:             # deleting the one-shot here would make the documented
4077:             # resume-on-policy-loosening semantic impossible for at-jobs.
4078:             # A run that never STARTED is the same story for a different reason --
4079:             # every pool worker was busy for the whole queue budget -- so consuming
4080:             # the one-shot would destroy scheduled work that never got a chance to
4081:             # run. Only the delete is suppressed: unlike a policy denial this needs
4082:             # no operator action, so the job stays enabled and simply retries.
4083:             # TWO signals, because the queue and the audit ask different
4084:             # questions and a corrupt store answers them differently.
4085:             #   delete_owed      -- is a consume OWED by this path at all?
4086:             #   removed_one_shot -- did this path actually remove a PRESENT job?
4087:             # Deriving both from presence conflated them: `_load` degrades an
4088:             # unreadable store to an empty job list WITHOUT raising, so presence
4089:             # is exactly what a corrupt store destroys, and the deferred queue
4090:             # below then never fired for a delete that was still owed on disk.
4091:             delete_owed = job.delete_after_run and not (
4092:                 job.fire_time_denied or job.run_never_started
4093:             )

466: def compute_jitter(job: CronJob) -> float:
467:     """Return random jitter seconds based on schedule frequency.
468: 
469:     - strict_schedule=True or one-shot 'at' jobs: no jitter
470:     - Sub-hourly (every < 3600s or cron whose parsed minute field fires
471:       more than once per hour): no jitter
472:     - Hourly (every 3600–86399s or cron firing hourly): 0–5 min
473:     - Daily (every >= 86400s or cron firing daily): 0–59 min
474:     - Unrecognized cron patterns (fallback): 0–5 min
475:     """
476:     if job.strict_schedule:
477:         return 0.0
478:     sched = job.schedule
479:     if sched.kind == "at":
480:         return 0.0  # one-shot jobs fire at exact time
481:     if sched.kind == "every" and sched.every_secs:
482:         if sched.every_secs >= 86400:
483:             return random.uniform(0, _JITTER_DAILY_MAX)
484:         elif sched.every_secs >= 3600:
485:             return random.uniform(0, _JITTER_HOURLY_MAX)
486:         else:
487:             return 0.0  # sub-hourly jobs shouldn't be jittered
488:     if sched.kind == "cron" and sched.cron_expr:
489:         # Ask croniter for the normalized minute set. Wildcard collapses
490:         # to ["*"]; lists, ranges, steps, and their combinations expand
491:         # and deduplicate, so cardinality reflects actual fires per hour.
492:         try:
493:             expanded, _ = croniter.expand(sched.cron_expr)
494:             minute_values = expanded[0]
495:         except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
496:             minute_values = []
497:         if minute_values == ["*"] or len(minute_values) > 1:
498:             return 0.0
499: 
500:         parts = sched.cron_expr.split()
501:         if len(parts) == 5:
502:             # Single literal hour (e.g., "0 3 * * *") = truly daily/weekly
503:             if parts[1].isdigit():
504:                 return random.uniform(0, _JITTER_DAILY_MAX)
505:             # Multi-hour patterns (*/2, 1,13) or wildcard = hourly jitter
506:             if parts[1] != "*":
507:                 return random.uniform(0, _JITTER_HOURLY_MAX)
508:         return random.uniform(0, _JITTER_HOURLY_MAX)
509:     return 0.0

512: def is_due(job: CronJob, now: float) -> bool:
513:     """Whether ``job`` is due at ``now``: its schedule has arrived and ``now`` is not a skip date."""
514:     from kiro_crew import cron as seams  # the facade holds the patched names; it imports us
515: 
516:     if job.schedule.kind == "every" and job.schedule.every_secs:
517:         last = job.last_run_ts or job.created_ts
518:         if now < last + job.schedule.every_secs:
519:             return False
520:     elif job.schedule.kind == "at" and job.schedule.at_ts:
521:         if now < job.schedule.at_ts:
522:             return False
523:     elif job.schedule.kind == "cron" and job.schedule.cron_expr:
524:         tz = _job_tz(job)
525:         dt = seams.datetime.fromtimestamp(now, tz=tz)
526:         if not seams.cron_expr_matches(job.schedule.cron_expr, dt):
527:             return False
528:         # Don't re-fire within the same UTC minute (immune to DST ambiguity)
529:         if job.last_run_ts and int(job.last_run_ts) // 60 == int(now) // 60:
530:             return False
531:     else:
532:         return False
533:     # Skip dates check (evaluated in job's local timezone, applies to all schedule types)
534:     if job.skip_dates:
535:         local_date = seams.datetime.fromtimestamp(now, _job_tz(job)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
536:         if local_date in job.skip_dates:
537:             return False
538:     return True
